Subject: Residency & training assurances — quick confirmation

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning. Two quick confirmations FinServe needs for procurement:

1) Contract language we can point to that says Redwood will not use customer input data to update or train any production models (including offline training or fine-tuning) without explicit, documented consent.
2) Practical retention nuances: what exactly gets retained (logs, KV cache, snapshots, backups), for how long, and what deletion evidence you can provide (timestamps, deletion logs, manifest entries). We need these details ahead of the legal review.

Could you either provide the contractual excerpt or point me to evidence of the deletion path? If there are EU-specific residency caveats (e.g., backups in a different region for DR), call that out.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we have an internal deadline Friday.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency & training assurances — quick confirmation

Hi Elliot — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- Contractual pledge: Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train, fine-tune, or improve production models unless the customer has explicitly opted in via a signed SOW/addendum. We will provide a DPA addendum clause you can drop into your contract.

- Retention & deletion evidence: we retain request/response traces and operational logs for a short window for debugging and abuse detection, and we retain longer-term snapshots/backups for DR. We can provide deletion manifests and timestamped logs for customer data on request.

Details below and an evidence pack attached (DPA_Redwood_2029.pdf + snapshot-deletion-playbook_v1.txt).

--- Detailed notes ---
What we DO NOT do by default:
- We do NOT use customer input or customer-generated inference results to update any general-purpose production models, retrain base models, or add to any open training corpus without documented customer consent.

What we DO process and why:
- Request payloads / responses: processed in-memory for inference. Short-lived traces are written to ephemeral logs to support tracing, billing, and debugging.
- KV cache / prefix caches: stored per-tenant to accelerate repeated requests. Cached items follow the tenant TTL and are separate from global model artifacts.
- Operational logs (auth, routing, throttling): retained for security and billing reconciliation.
- Backups & snapshots: periodic encrypted snapshots for disaster recovery; these are the most likely place where deleted content might persist beyond primary TTLs.

Typical retention windows (defaults, configurable in contract):
- Ephemeral request traces: 30 days (can be reduced to 7 days under enterprise config).
- Operational logs: 90 days standard (longer retention available for auditing via paid retention add-on).
- Backups/snapshots: rolling snapshots retained up to 180 days by default; we can implement shorter windows or customer-managed snapshot TTLs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Deletion & evidence workflow:
1) Customer requests deletion (portal or API) -> triggers: mark for purge, remove live objects, invalidate caches.
2) Background job scans and removes items from primary stores within 24–72 hours depending on volume.
3) Snapshot purge: included in next snapshot cycle; manifests updated with tombstone entries.
4) Final proof: we can provide a signed deletion manifest (S3 object keys + deletion timestamps + service job IDs) and an audit log extract showing the purge run id.

EU residency notes:
- Hosted (multi-region): we keep primary processing in the region you select (e.g., eu-west-1). However, DR backups may be stored in a different region by default; this is configurable for enterprise contracts.
- Private/VPC deployments: customer can opt for fully region-restricted storage; snapshots and backups remain in-customer-region.

Evidence we can provide with the DPA package:
- DPA clause excerpt (explicit no-train warranty unless opted in)
- Snapshot deletion playbook (steps and expected timing)
- Sample signed deletion manifest (redacted)
- SOC2 audit references and contact for compliance evidence requests

Next steps: Priyom (ops) — can you confirm the snapshot TTL options and the manifest fields we’ll include for FinServe? Marissa — I’m copying you to keep Solutions in the loop.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Lauren / Marissa,

Thanks for the rapid response. A few follow-ups from our side before we advance to redlines:

1) We need explicit contract text that says "Redwood warrants it will not use Customer Data to train or improve any machine learning models used in production unless Customer provides written consent." Please supply the exact clause you intend to include in the DPA.

2) Deletion evidence: the legal team wants to see a sample deletion manifest with at least the following fields: object key / path, UTC deletion timestamp, deletion job id, responsible service account, and an attest signature (or hash). The sample Lauren mentioned should be sufficient if it contains real field names (redacted values ok).

3) Snapshots/backups: confirm whether snapshot metadata is retained separately from snapshot objects (we prefer metadata tombstoning so the exact object is not recoverable). If backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK), confirm whether you can revoke keys for an immediate crypto-sweep.

Please reply by EOD tomorrow to keep us on track.

Regards,
FinServe Legal

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: FinServe Legal <legal@finserve.com>, Elliot Martin <elliot.martin@finserve.com>

Subject: Re: Residency & training assurances — quick confirmation

Hi Elliot and team — looping back with the specifics you requested. Below is the exact language we propose for the DPA (you can paste into your contract):

--- Proposed DPA language (editable) ---
"Redwood warrants and represents that, except where Customer has provided explicit, documented, and auditable consent in writing, Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models that are part of Redwood's production services. Any use for training will be subject to a separate agreement detailing scope, compensation, and data handling controls."

Sample deletion manifest fields we will provide (redacted example included in the attached playbook):
- object_key: s3://redwood-prod/finserve/accounts/12345/session-abc123.log
- deletion_timestamp_utc: 2029-05-16T18:12:24Z
- deletion_job_id: purge-job-20290516-47b9
- service_account: ops-deletion@redwood-service
- manifest_signature: sha256:3f5b... (we provide hash + signing key reference)

Snapshots & CMK notes:
- Snapshot metadata: we tombstone metadata entries on deletion runs; we mark snapshots as deleted and remove pointers during the purge cycle. The physical snapshot object is removed on next snapshot compaction cycle (within configured TTL).
- CMK: for Dedicated/Private customers we offer CMK options. Revoking a CMK will render snapshot objects unreadable (crypto-sweep) but we still provide a deletion manifest showing key revocation timestamp and key-id. For Hosted customers we can support vendor-managed CMKs and contractually require region-locking for EU deployments.

Evidence pack we can share immediately (redacted):
- Redacted deletion manifest sample (attached)
- Snapshot deletion playbook (attached)
- DPA excerpt (attached)
- Instructions for a signed attestation (we can produce a signed letter on company letterhead after contract signature)

If you'd like, we can produce an automated deletion-run export for a test dataset and deliver it to your secure share so you can validate the manifest format.

Lauren / Marissa — happy to take this offline if you want a mini technical walkthrough for FinServe.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
